# incident_grouping_preference (Resource)

How alerts are grouped: the organisation default, or one team's preference. Alert rules group
an alert by the first branch whose conditions hold, else by the default. Alert routes only use a
team's default.

The organisation has one default (`scope = "organisation"`), and a plan that creates it fails once it
exists: import it by ID instead. Destroying it turns its grouping off and hands it back to the
dashboard. Each team has at most one preference (`scope = "team"`), created and deleted like any other
resource. A preference can't change scope or move to another team, so a plan that changes `scope` or
`team_id` fails.

A team's default can be written whatever your organisation routes alerts with. Its branches, and
anything about the organisation default, can only be changed once your organisation has moved to
alert rules. Until then the API refuses the change and this resource fails at apply with that message.

This replaces `incident_team_grouping_preference`. To move one over without recreating it, on
Terraform 1.8 or later, add `scope = "team"` and a `moved` block:

```terraform
moved {
  from = incident_team_grouping_preference.payments
  to   = incident_grouping_preference.payments
}
```

On earlier versions, run `terraform state rm` on the old address and import the preference into
this resource by its ID. The old resource left the team's branches and expressions as the dashboard
wrote them, but this one manages them: declare any the team has, or the next apply removes them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The organisation default groups every alert that no team's preference groups. Alert
# rules use the first branch whose conditions hold, else the default.
resource "incident_grouping_preference" "organisation" {
  scope = "organisation"

  default = {
    settings = {
      enabled        = true
      window_type    = "rolling"
      window_seconds = 1800
      grouping_keys  = [{ reference = "alert.title" }]
    }
  }

  # Database alerts group in a shorter window.
  branch {
    condition_groups = [{
      conditions = [{
        subject        = "alert.title"
        operation      = "contains"
        param_bindings = [{ value_literal = "database" }]
      }]
    }]

    settings = {
      enabled        = true
      window_type    = "fixed"
      window_seconds = 600
    }
  }
}

# A team's preference groups that team's alerts. Teams are catalog entries of your Team
# type, so look the team up rather than hardcoding its ID.
data "incident_catalog_type" "team" {
  name = "Team"
}

data "incident_catalog_entry" "payments" {
  catalog_type_id = data.incident_catalog_type.team.id
  identifier      = "Payments"
}

resource "incident_grouping_preference" "payments" {
  scope   = "team"
  team_id = data.incident_catalog_entry.payments.id

  # None of the team's alerts group, unless a branch below matches. Disabled settings carry
  # no window or keys.
  default = {
    settings = {
      enabled = false
    }
  }

  branch {
    condition_groups = [{
      conditions = [{
        subject        = "alert.title"
        operation      = "is_set"
        param_bindings = []
      }]
    }]

    settings = {
      enabled        = true
      window_type    = "rolling"
      window_seconds = 900
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `default` (Attributes) The grouping settings for alerts no branch matches. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default))
- `scope` (String) Whether this is the organisation default or a team's preference. Possible values are: `organisation`, `team`. It can't change.

### Optional

- `branch` (Block List) Grouping branches in order. Alert rules group an alert by the first branch whose conditions hold, else by the default. Alert routes only use the default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--branch))
- `named_expression` (Block List) An expression this resource owns, addressed by name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--named_expression))
- `team_id` (String) The catalog entry ID of the team this preference belongs to. Required when `scope` is `team`, and not allowed otherwise. It can't change.
- `unlock_in_dashboard` (Boolean) Whether to leave this resource unlocked in the incident.io dashboard, so people can edit it there. Defaults to `false`: Terraform claims what it manages, and a claimed resource cannot be edited in the dashboard. Set it to `true` to leave the resource unclaimed — pair that with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [...] }` naming the attributes people edit, or the next apply reverts them. Setting it on a resource Terraform already claimed hands that resource back, and someone disconnecting one in the dashboard shows as no change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this preference
- `version` (Number) The current version number, incremented on each update

<a id="nestedatt--default"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default`

Required:

- `settings` (Attributes) How alerts are grouped together (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default--settings))

<a id="nestedatt--default--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default.settings`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether these alerts are grouped. When false, none of them are grouped.

Optional:

- `ai_enabled` (Boolean) Use AI to group similar looking alerts. AI alert grouping can only group alerts that are attributed to the same team, so grouping keys must be empty or only contain the team alert attribute. Private alerts are not grouped unless AI incident access allows private incidents and alerts. Omit it on an update to keep the current value.
- `grouping_keys` (Attributes Set) Which alert attributes the team's alerts are grouped by. Only set when grouping is enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default--settings--grouping_keys))
- `window_seconds` (Number) How long the grouping window is, in seconds. Must be between 60 (1 minute) and 172800 (48 hours). Only set when grouping is enabled.
- `window_type` (String) How the grouping window behaves. 'rolling' keeps the window open for window_seconds after the most recent alert, so the group stays open as long as alerts keep arriving. 'fixed' opens the window when the first alert arrives and always closes window_seconds later. Only set when grouping is enabled. Possible values are: `rolling`, `fixed`.

Required:

- `reference` (String) A reference to a property of the alert to group on

Required:

- `settings` (Attributes) How alerts are grouped together (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--branch--settings))

Optional:

<a id="nestedblock--named_expression--operation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `named_expression.operation`

Optional:

- `branches` (Block, Optional) A lookup table, evaluated in order until one matches. Must be the only operation in its expression, with start_from = ".". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--named_expression--operation--branches))
- `cast` (Attributes) Converts the current value to another type. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--cast))
- `concatenate` (Attributes) Adds the values behind another reference to the current value, keeping each value once. There is no delimiter, despite the name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--concatenate))
- `count` (Attributes) Counts the values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--count))
- `filter` (Attributes) Keeps the values matching these conditions. Inside a filter the value under test is bound as `input`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--filter))
- `first` (Attributes) Takes the first value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--first))
- `max` (Attributes) Takes the largest value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--max))
- `min` (Attributes) Takes the smallest value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--min))
- `navigate` (Attributes) Follows an attribute of the current value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--navigate))
- `parse` (Attributes) Evaluates a function against the current value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--parse))
- `random` (Attributes) Takes one value at random. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--random))
- `sum` (Attributes) Adds the values together. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--sum))

## Import

Import is supported using an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) or the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import):

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash

# Import a team's grouping preference or the organisation default using its ID. Replace the
# ID with a real ID from your incident.io organization: the public API's team grouping
# preferences endpoint lists each team's, filtered by team_id, and its default grouping
# preferences endpoint returns the organisation default. Creating the default fails once it
# exists, so this is how Terraform takes it over.
terraform import incident_grouping_preference.example 01ABC123DEF456GHI789JKL
```
